Section 1: Concept of Programming (Questions 1 to 25)

Q1. Which of the following is the lowest level of programming language?

A) High-Level Language B) Assembly Language C) Machine Language ✅ D) Structured Language

Q2. Which language uses mnemonics like ADD, MOV, SUB?

A) Machine Language B) Assembly Language ✅ C) C Language D) Java

Q3. What is the main advantage of High-Level Languages?

A) Faster execution B) Easier to understand and write ✅ C) Uses less memory D) No need for compilers

Q4. Which of the following is NOT a high-level language?

A) Python B) Java C) Assembly ✅ D) C++

Q5. What is the difference between an instruction and a program?

A) Instruction is a single command, program is a set of instructions ✅ B) Instruction is a set, program is a single command C) Both are the same D) Instruction is used only in machine language

Q6. Which of the following is an example of a program?

A) int x = 5; B) A word processor application ✅ C) A single printf statement D) A flowchart

Q7. What is the role of a compiler?

A) To execute the program directly B) To convert high-level code to machine code ✅ C) To design algorithms D) To test the program

Q8. Which of the following is TRUE about assembly language?

A) It is machine-independent B) It uses mnemonics for operations ✅ C) It is easier than high-level languages D) It does not need translation

Q9. What is the advantage of machine language?

A) Easy to understand B) Fast execution ✅ C) Portable D) Easy to debug

Q10. Which programming paradigm focuses on functions and procedures?

A) Object-Oriented Programming B) Procedural Programming ✅ C) Non-Procedural Programming D) Functional Programming

Q11. Which of the following is a characteristic of Procedural Programming?

A) Data is hidden B) Programs are organized around functions ✅ C) Uses inheritance D) Uses polymorphism

Q12. What is the main focus of Object-Oriented Programming?

A) Functions B) Data and objects ✅ C) Procedures D) Algorithms

Q13. Which of the following is NOT a principle of OOP?

A) Encapsulation B) Inheritance C) Polymorphism D) Recursion ✅

Q14. What is encapsulation in OOP?

A) Combining data and methods into a single unit ✅ B) Creating multiple classes C) Using many functions D) Hiding all code

Q15. What is inheritance in OOP?

A) Reusing code by deriving new classes from existing ones ✅ B) Creating multiple objects C) Defining many functions D) Using pointers

Q16. Which of the following languages supports OOP?

A) C B) FORTRAN C) C++ ✅ D) Assembly

Q17. What is the difference between Structured Programming and OOP?

A) Structured uses objects, OOP uses functions B) Structured uses functions and data separately, OOP combines them ✅ C) Both are same D) Structured is newer

Q18. Which concept in OOP allows one interface to be used for multiple data types?

A) Encapsulation B) Inheritance C) Polymorphism ✅ D) Abstraction

Q19. What is abstraction in OOP?

A) Hiding implementation details and showing only functionality ✅ B) Creating many objects C) Using multiple inheritance D) Writing many functions

Q20. Which of the following is a non-procedural language?

A) C B) Pascal C) SQL ✅ D) FORTRAN

Q21. In non-procedural languages, what is the programmer's focus?

A) How to do a task B) What to do ✅ C) Memory management D) Function definitions

Q22. Which of the following is a characteristic of Structured Programming?

A) Top-down design ✅ B) Use of goto statements C) Global variables only D) No functions

Q23. Who introduced the concept of Structured Programming?

A) Dennis Ritchie B) Edsger Dijkstra ✅ C) James Gosling D) Alan Turing

Q24. Which of the following is NOT a feature of Structured Programming?

A) Sequence B) Selection C) Iteration D) Inheritance ✅

Q25. What is the main disadvantage of low-level languages?

A) Hard to understand and write ✅ B) Slow execution C) Cannot control hardware D) They are not portable

Section 2: Algorithm Fundamentals (Questions 26 to 80)

Q26. An algorithm must have which of the following?

A) Infinite steps B) No inputs C) Finiteness ✅ D) No output

Q27. What does "definiteness" in an algorithm mean?

A) The algorithm must produce some output B) Each step must be precisely defined ✅ C) The algorithm must be short D) The algorithm must be recursive

Q28. What is the output of an algorithm?

A) The result of the problem being solved ✅ B) The input data C) The code D) The algorithm itself

Q29. Which of the following is an example of a recursive algorithm?

A) Sum of array elements using a loop B) Binary search using recursion ✅ C) Finding max using if-else D) Swapping two numbers

Q30. In recursion, what is the role of the recursive case?

A) Terminates the recursion B) Calls the function again with smaller problem ✅ C) Prints the output D) Defines the base case

Q31. What is the main disadvantage of recursion?

A) Code is longer B) More memory and time overhead due to stack ✅ C) Not suitable for any problems D) Cannot be implemented in C

Q32. What is a flowchart's purpose?

A) To represent an algorithm graphically ✅ B) To write actual code C) To execute a program D) To store data

Q33. Which symbol is used for processing in a flowchart?

A) Rectangle ✅ B) Diamond C) Oval D) Parallelogram

Q34. Which symbol is used for a loop in a flowchart?

A) Rectangle B) Diamond (decision) ✅ (loops are represented by decisions) C) Oval D) Parallelogram

Q35. What does a parallelogram represent in a flowchart?

A) Start/End B) Decision C) Input/Output ✅ D) Processing

Q36. What is pseudo-code?

A) A high-level programming language B) A mix of natural language and programming constructs ✅ C) Machine code D) A type of flowchart

Q37. Which of the following is an advantage of pseudo-code?

A) It can be executed directly B) It is independent of any programming language ✅ C) It is faster than code D) It uses less memory

Q38. What is the time complexity of sequential search?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q39. What is the time complexity of binary search?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(n log n)

Q40. Which of the following has the highest time complexity?

A) O(1) B) O(log n) C) O(n) D) O(n²) ✅

Q41. What does O(n²) mean?

A) Running time increases linearly B) Running time increases quadratically ✅ C) Running time is constant D) Running time increases logarithmically

Q42. Which complexity notation is used to express the average-case performance?

A) Big O B) Big Omega C) Big Theta ✅ D) Little o

Q43. What is the worst-case time complexity of insertion sort?

A) O(n) B) O(n²) ✅ C) O(log n) D) O(n log n)

Q44. What is the best-case time complexity of insertion sort?

A) O(n) ✅ B) O(n²) C) O(log n) D) O(n log n)

Q45. What is the time complexity of quick sort in the worst case?

A) O(n log n) B) O(n²) ✅ C) O(n) D) O(log n)

Q46. What is the time complexity of quick sort in the average case?

A) O(n²) B) O(n log n) ✅ C) O(n) D) O(log n)

Q47. Which sorting algorithm has a time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases?

A) Bubble sort B) Selection sort C) Merge sort ✅ D) Quick sort (worst case)

Q48. What is the space complexity of merge sort?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q49. Which asymptotic notation gives the tightest bound?

A) Big O B) Big Omega C) Big Theta ✅ D) Little omega

Q50. What is the time complexity of reading an element from an array by index?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(1) ✅ D) O(n²)

Q51. What is the time complexity of inserting an element at the end of a linked list (if you have a tail pointer)?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(n) C) O(log n) D) O(n²)

Q52. What is the time complexity of searching in a sorted array using binary search?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(n log n)

Q53. What does Big Omega notation describe?

A) Upper bound B) Lower bound ✅ C) Exact bound D) Average bound

Q54. What is the purpose of algorithm analysis?

A) To make the code longer B) To estimate resource usage ✅ C) To add more comments D) To make the program unreadable

Q55. What is the time complexity of a while loop that runs log n times?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(1) D) O(n²)

Q56. What is the time complexity of a loop that runs n/2 times?

A) O(n) ✅ B) O(n/2) (but we drop constants, so O(n)) C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q57. What is the time complexity of nested loops where outer runs n and inner runs m?

A) O(n+m) B) O(n*m) ✅ C) O(n) D) O(m)

Q58. What is the space complexity of an iterative binary search?

A) O(1) ✅ B) O(log n) C) O(n) D) O(n²)

Q59. What is the space complexity of a recursive binary search?

A) O(1) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(n) D) O(n²)

Q60. Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a good algorithm?

A) Definiteness B) Finiteness C) Ambiguity ✅ D) Effectiveness

Q61. What is an "effective" step in an algorithm?

A) A step that is vague B) A step that can be performed exactly and in a finite time ✅ C) A step that uses recursion D) A step that has no output

Q62. What is the difference between an algorithm and a program?

A) Algorithm is human-readable, program is machine-readable ✅ B) Program is human-readable, algorithm is machine-readable C) Both are the same D) Algorithm is written in a language, program is not

Q63. What is the time complexity of finding the minimum element in an unsorted array?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q64. What is the time complexity of matrix multiplication (Strassen's algorithm)?

A) O(n³) B) O(n².81) ✅ (approx) C) O(n log n) D) O(n)

Q65. Which growth rate is faster?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) C) O(n²) ✅ D) O(n log n)

Q66. What is the time complexity of factorial using iteration?

A) O(1) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q67. What is the time complexity of Fibonacci using dynamic programming?

A) O(2ⁿ) B) O(n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(n log n)

Q68. What is the space complexity of Fibonacci using dynamic programming?

A) O(1) ✅ (if using only two variables) B) O(n) C) O(n²) D) O(log n)

Q69. What is the primary use of a flowchart?

A) To write code B) To design and document algorithms visually ✅ C) To execute programs D) To test programs

Q70. What is a decision box in a flowchart used for?

A) To perform calculations B) To make a decision based on a condition ✅ C) To input data D) To output results

Q71. Which of the following is a correct pseudo-code representation of a loop?

A) for i = 1 to n do ✅ B) loop i = 1..n C) repeat i from 1 to n D) while (i <= n)

Q72. What does the term "space-time tradeoff" mean?

A) Using more memory to reduce time or vice versa ✅ B) Using no memory and no time C) Using the same memory and time D) Using less memory and more time

Q73. Which algorithm design technique divides the problem into smaller subproblems?

A) Greedy B) Divide and Conquer ✅ C) Dynamic Programming D) Brute Force

Q74. Which of the following is a recursive algorithm design technique?

A) Divide and Conquer ✅ B) Iteration C) Greedy D) Brute Force

Q75. What is the time complexity of Tower of Hanoi (recurrence T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1)?

A) O(n) B) O(2ⁿ) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(n log n)

Q76. What is the time complexity of exponentiation by squaring (fast power)?

A) O(n) B) O(log n) ✅ C) O(n²) D) O(2ⁿ)

Q77. What is the recurrence for binary search?

A) T(n) = T(n-1) + 1 B) T(n) = T(n/2) + 1 ✅ C) T(n) = 2T(n/2) + 1 D) T(n) = T(n/2) + n

Q78. What does Big Theta notation represent?

A) Both upper and lower bounds ✅ B) Only upper bound C) Only lower bound D) Average case

Q79. Which asymptotic notation is used for the best-case running time?

A) Big O B) Big Omega ✅ C) Big Theta D) Little o

Q80. Which of the following is not a valid asymptotic notation?

A) O(n) B) Ω(n) C) Θ(n) D) Δ(n) ✅

Section 3: Introduction to Problem Solving (Questions 81 to 100)

Q81. What is the first step in the problem-solving process?

A) Implementation B) Algorithm development C) Problem understanding ✅ D) Debugging

Q82. What is the role of algorithm development?

A) To write code B) To design a step-by-step solution ✅ C) To test the program D) To fix errors

Q83. What is the last step in problem solving?

A) Analysis B) Algorithm C) Coding D) Testing and Debugging ✅

Q84. What is the purpose of testing?

A) To write the program B) To find and fix errors ✅ C) To design the algorithm D) To analyze the problem

Q85. Which step involves converting the algorithm into a specific programming language?

A) Problem analysis B) Algorithm design C) Coding ✅ D) Testing

Q86. What is debugging?

A) Writing code B) Testing the program C) Identifying and removing errors ✅ D) Designing the algorithm

Q87. What is the difference between a syntax error and a runtime error?

A) Syntax error occurs during compilation, runtime error occurs during execution ✅ B) Both occur during execution C) Both occur during compilation D) Runtime error is easier to fix

Q88. What is a logical error?

A) A violation of language rules B) The program runs but produces wrong output ✅ C) A memory error D) A division by zero

Q89. Which of the following is a tool used for debugging?

A) Compiler B) Debugger ✅ C) Linker D) Interpreter

Q90. What is the importance of problem analysis?

A) It helps in writing code faster B) It ensures clear understanding of requirements ✅ C) It tests the program D) It generates errors

Q91. What is the difference between testing and debugging?

A) Testing finds errors, debugging fixes them ✅ B) Testing fixes errors, debugging finds them C) Both are the same D) Testing is done before coding

Q92. What is unit testing?

A) Testing the entire system B) Testing individual components ✅ C) Testing the algorithm D) Testing the user interface

Q93. What is integration testing?

A) Testing individual modules B) Testing combined modules together ✅ C) Testing the complete system D) Testing the database

Q94. What is the main goal of problem solving?

A) To write as much code as possible B) To create a correct and efficient solution ✅ C) To add more features D) To make the program complex

Q95. Which step is most time-consuming in problem solving?

A) Analysis B) Algorithm design C) Coding D) Testing and Debugging ✅

Q96. What is the purpose of pseudo-code in problem solving?

A) To execute directly B) To plan the algorithm before coding ✅ C) To test the program D) To generate machine code

Q97. What is a flowchart used for?

A) To execute the program B) To visualize the algorithm steps ✅ C) To store data D) To compile code

Q98. What is the final output of the problem-solving process?

A) An algorithm B) A flowchart C) A working program ✅ D) A pseudo-code

Q99. What is the role of an IDE in problem solving?

A) To design algorithms B) To provide tools for coding, testing, and debugging ✅ C) To analyze problems D) To generate pseudo-code

Q100. Which of the following is TRUE about the problem-solving process?

A) It is linear and never requires iteration B) It may require going back to previous steps (iterative) ✅ C) Testing is not important D) Analysis is optional
